title: Split a large file into modules
when: A single script has grown into hundreds of lines and the user wants it organized into several modules.
inputs: how it is loaded (script tag, node entry point)
prompt:
Goal: A few cohesive ES modules with explicit imports and exports, loaded the same way, with identical behavior.
Steps:
1. Group the top level code by responsibility: state, pure logic, storage, rendering, event wiring, startup.
2. Draw the dependency direction first: logic imports nothing from rendering; rendering may import logic; main imports all.
3. Move each group to its own file (state.js, logic.js, storage.js, view.js, main.js) and export only what other files use.
4. Replace shared globals with exported functions or a single state object passed in.
5. In the browser load only main.js with <script type="module" src="main.js"></script>; in Node use relative imports with the .js extension.
6. Remove the old file content once every function has a single home.
Quality bar:
- No circular imports.
- Each module has one reason to change.
- Import paths are relative and include the extension.
Pitfalls:
- Module scripts opened from file:// may be blocked; note that a local server is needed.
- Leaving copies of the same function in two files.
- Exporting everything by default, which hides the real interface.
Verify:
- [ ] Every import name is exported by its target.
- [ ] The page or script starts without errors.
- [ ] No file over about 300 lines remains.
- [ ] main.js is the only entry point.
Output: The new module files, the updated HTML script tag or entry point, and a one line map of what each file owns.

examples.output: state.js, todo-logic.js, storage.js, view.js and main.js with type="module"
